## Summary

**VPERM** (Vector Permute): Permute the contents of two registers into destination register.

## Details

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Operation | `Pick bytes from a & b → d` |
| Syntax | `VPERM #n,a,b,d`<br>where #n contains the picking order from a & b |
| Short | Permute the contents of two registers into destination register. |
| Constraints | The operands a, b & d must be data registers. |
| Condition codes | not affected |

### Encoding

| Word | Bits | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15–9 | `1111111` |
| 1 | 8 | A |
| 1 | 7 | B |
| 1 | 6 | D |
| 1 | 5–0 | `111111` |
| 2 | 15–12 | b |
| 2 | 11–8 | d |
| 2 | 7–4 | `0000` |
| 2 | 3–0 | a |
| 3 | 15–12 | pos0 |
| 3 | 11–8 | pos1 |
| 3 | 7–4 | pos2 |
| 3 | 3–0 | pos3 |
| 4 | 15–12 | pos4 |
| 4 | 11–8 | pos5 |
| 4 | 7–4 | pos6 |
| 4 | 3–0 | pos7 |

### Example

```asm
    vperm    #$3210AB78,d0,e1,e6
```

```text
a d0: 00 11 22 33 44 55 66 77
b e1: 88 99 AA BB CC DD EE FF
Result:
d e6: 33 22 11 00 AA BB 77 88
```

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- The 68000–68060 have no VPERM. It is new on the 68080.

## Do / Don't

- DO use data registers for a, b and d.
